control_flow: followInTheDark: if LLIGHT < 70 (dark) check the line tracker: below 90 curve left 10/30, above 90 curve right 30/10, exactly 90 call avoidWalls; if bright call avoidWalls.
avoidWalls: if dark, LEFT obstacle turn right 20, ELSE RIGHT obstacle turn left 20, else driveInTheDark; if bright call driveInTheDark.
driveInTheDark: if dark drive forward 30 %; if bright call stopAtWall.
stopAtWall: if an obstacle is ahead stop; else call followLine.
followLine: if the line tracker sees black curve left 10/40; else curve right 40/10.

scenarios.coded_response: In the dark it curves left on black or peach and right on the white band; after the exit it follows the line in bright light.
scenarios.initial_condition: The robot is on a black line in dim light, inside a tunnel, with the line running on through the exit.
scenarios.trigger: In the dark the line tracker sees black and the white band again and again.
scenarios.title: Follows the line in the dark
assumptions: The line runs on through the tunnel and ends where the robot should get to.
scenarios.expected_response_hypothesis: It follows the line through the dark tunnel and reaches the line's end after the exit.

scenarios.coded_response: It curves left when it sees black and right otherwise, following the line.
scenarios.initial_condition: The robot is on or beside a black line in bright light, with no tunnel.
scenarios.trigger: The line tracker sees black and no black again and again.
scenarios.title: Follows the line in bright light
assumptions: Saying 'in the dark too' means the robot should also follow the line in bright light.
scenarios.expected_response_hypothesis: It follows the line to its end.

scenarios.coded_response: It stops while an obstacle is ahead and stays stopped.
scenarios.initial_condition: The robot follows a black line in bright light and a wall stands across the line.
scenarios.trigger: The front obstacle sensor sees the wall.
scenarios.title: Stops at a wall on the line
assumptions: You didn't say what to do at a wall; your program stops, so I took that as intended.
scenarios.expected_response_hypothesis: It stops before the wall without bumping into it.

uncertainties: In the dark your program reads only the line tracker, not the obstacle sensors: if the line runs into a tunnel wall, it bumps instead of turning.
The middle branch 'line tracker exactly 90 %' can't be reached in a test: 90 % happens only for a moment at a line's edge.
The dark branches of avoidWalls and driveInTheDark can never run, because both are only called in bright light.
